key_insight: English-language eligibility requirements became more common in US clinical trials and were associated with a lower enrolled proportion of Asian participants.
clinical_relevance: Reviewing language requirements and accommodations may help sponsors address barriers to representative trial enrollment, though this study does not establish causality.
method: Cross-sectional analysis of 44,487 interventional trials with exclusively US sites and posted results on ClinicalTrials.gov.
Classified language requirements and accommodations from eligibility text using rules validated against physician review.
Modeled trial-level racial and ethnic composition with adjustment for trial characteristics and geographic population composition.
evidence_signal: English requirements appeared in 12.9% of trials and documented accommodations in 1.8%; requirements were associated with lower Asian enrollment proportions (adjusted OR 0.85, 95% CI 0.77–0.93).
watch_item: Race and ethnicity reporting was incomplete, and the supplied abstract is truncated; this is trial-inclusivity research, not an AI cancer drug-discovery study.
paper_title: Language eligibility criteria and enrolled racial and ethnic composition in US clinical trials: a cross-sectional study
